scenes.say: Fresh beans can make great filter coffee and a difficult espresso. The reason is a gas left behind by roasting.
Fresher coffee doesn't always make a better espresso. Right after roasting, beans are still full of carbon dioxide, and that gas gets in the way of the shot.

scenes.title: The espresso problem.
scenes.say: Beans release this gas slowly after roasting. In espresso, water is pushed through fine coffee in seconds, so the trapped gas fights back and the shot can taste sour.

scenes.title: Filter is gentler.
scenes.say: In filter coffee, water drips through slowly with no pressure. Most of the gas escapes during the bloom, the first small pour that makes the grounds bubble.

scenes.title: The tip.
scenes.say: With a very fresh bag, brew filter first. Wait a few more days before espresso, because the gas needs time to leave.
Espresso wants rested beans, while filter handles fresh ones better thanks to the bloom. Save this for your next bag.
